title: Pair adjudication — quick protocols and triage cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference for two-person adjudication sessions (pair labeling) when a single example is ambiguous. Meant for labelers and the first-line adjudicator. Keep this on your monitor during pairing runs. This is intentionally compact — expanded rationale is in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-Labeling-Playbook-6789).

When to invoke pair adjudication (quick rules):
- If two independent labelers disagree and both options are plausible AND the example will be surfaced in training/qa (not throwaway).
- If the disagreement changes any metric or downstream routing (intent classification vs. fallback).
- If there is a repeated pattern of disagreement (>3 examples in the batch with same ambiguity).

Session setup (5 min):
- One labeler is "owner" of the pair session (starts the timer, files notes).
- Use the pairing channel thread (linked above) for quick context.
- Open the original ticket (JIRA-DATA-321) and the canonical guideline doc for quick checks.

Adjudication flow (target 2–4 minutes per example):
1) Read aloud the example and the two labels. No commentary beyond the facts.
2) Summarize the disagreement in one sentence (owner writes it). Example: "Disagree on whether 'they' refers to previous company or the author".
3) Quick evidence check (30–60s):
   - Search for explicit markers in the example (dates, punctuation, capitalization).
   - Check preceding n=2 context turns if available (we use n=2 default).
   - If model/system confuses numbered sequences (IDs, invoice lines), treat numeric ID patterns consistently (rule: keep as identifier unless natural-language intent).
4) Apply hard rules first (if applicable):
   - PII rules override subjective interpretation (if any PII present, label per PII guidance).
   - If text contains explicit role/title before name ("CEO Jane"), tag role-bound entity, not pronoun.
5) If no hard rule, use tie-break heuristic order:
   a) Literal reading (what the sentence strictly implies).
   b) Pragmatic reading (what a typical user would assume).
   c) Labeler confidence: if one labeler documents 3+ supporting tokens, prefer that label.
6) If still tied, create an "abstain/adjudicate later" flag and add one exemplar to the escalation queue (max 2 per session).

Example quick heuristics (copy these in the UI notes):
- Modifiers like "former" or "ex-" make role membership negative ("former manager" != manager).
- Date-like tokens without year: treat as temporal mention only if adjacent to verbs/time phrases.
- URLs with path fragments: prefer marking the domain as the entity, not the path, unless path contains readable slugs ("/pricing") which are product references.
- Currency + code ("USD 5k"): tag as currency-amount pair, not separate tokens.

Labeler ergonomics / keyboard shortcuts suggestions for speed:
- Toggle between candidate spans with tab (proposal to devs).
- Quick-save + add note = Ctrl+Enter (to capture adjudication rationale trace).
- Mark "needs context" checkbox when preceding >=2 turns are missing (this should auto-add to escalation queue).

Acceptance criteria: when recording the adjudicated label, include a one-line rationale and one canonical example (if applicable). Format: "reason: <short>, exemplar: <text snippet>". This is critical for downstream reviewer trust.

Common disagreement archetypes and recommended quick answers:
1) Overlapping spans: choose the longer meaningful span unless the extra tokens are determiners/prepositions. Example: "the CEO of Acme Corp" -> choose "CEO of Acme Corp" not just "CEO".
2) Nested entity vs attribute: if attribute attaches to entity type ("red 2015 Toyota"), entity="2015 Toyota" and attribute color="red"; but for current labeling round we prefer one primary span: "2015 Toyota" and add tag "has_color:red" only if structured schema allows.
3) Ambiguous pronouns with distant antecedents: prefer marking as "ambiguous_pronoun" when antecedent distance > 2 sentences.
4) Noise tokens and OCR artifacts: if >2 garbled tokens adjacent, mark as "uncertain" and require sample for dataset-cleanup batch.

Notes on partial labels and abstains:
- Partial labels are OK if the missing portion is trivial (determinants, trailing punctuation). Mark reason: "partial-ok".
- Abstain when >30% of the information needed is missing or corrupted. Abstain counts toward escalation queue.

Escalation rules (when to involve senior adjudicator):
- If a pattern appears in >5% of the batch and affects a downstream evaluation metric.
- If two adjudication sessions reach the same unresolved flag.
- If legal/PII ambiguity exists (immediately escalate).

Quick sampling checklist before closing a pair session (owner):
- Did we document rationales for all escalated examples? (Y/N)
- Did we tag each resolved example with one-line reason? (Y/N)
- Any guideline updates required? If yes, file quick note in Confluence with exemplar and proposed wording.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Should we formalize a 1–5 confidence score for each label to help probabilistic training? Pros: richer signal. Cons: annotator fatigue. (Priya to prototype 100-ex sample).
- Can we get a small keyboard UX patch for quick note capture (Ctrl+Enter)? Devs: Simon in dev-ux.
- Define default context-turns (n=2 is current informal rule). Need experiment to compare n=1 vs n=3 for precision on pronoun tasks. (Jamal to run A/B).

Quick exemplar log (these are anonymized, short):
- EX1: "They delivered the code yesterday; Alex will review if needed." Labels: "Alex" = person (both), Pronoun "They" = ambiguous (pair chose ambiguous_pronoun). Rationale: antecedent unclear and could refer to team.
- EX2: "Invoice INV-233/2021 shows credit to Acme Inc." Labels: invoice id vs free text: chose invoice id span INV-233/2021 (treat as identifier). Rationale: structured id semantics.
- EX3: "Set the endpoint to api.example.com/v1/chat for debug" Labels: endpoint = "api.example.com/v1/chat" (both). Rationale: path is human-readable and product-level.

Micro SOP for saving edits to central doc:
- Add a one-line change summary, tag with the session date, and add one exemplar. Avoid rephrasing global rules without example.

If you have more real-time friction, snap a 20–30s Loom and drop in thread. We iterate fast on small UX blockers.

— Elena M.
